snapshot_note: v0.53.0 released on develop 2026-07-26 - `-static-libmadc` now works in the .o LINK lane, lifting forest-carriers S5's last stated boundary. The AOT ledger is carried as MIR modules, so the pieces a program needs are pulled into a PRIVATE object-mode context, generated, emitted with MIR_gen_object_emit, and merged into the same builder as the .o inputs. Through the merge deliberately: a builder's symbol table is append-only (MIR_object_add_symbol never dedupes by name), and the unification that turns the inputs' UNDEF entries into references to the runtime's definitions IS the merge - so the runtime rides the ONE unification implementation, on the read-back path both containers (ELF ET_REL and MH_OBJECT) already gate. No new format code, no fork change. Generalized rather than duplicated: cir_ledger_pull takes a SEED list (the builder's UNDEF names join the module imports under the same not-defined filter), and the cover analysis takes the reference LIST rather than its source (source lanes pass context imports, the .o lane passes MIR_object_undef_name) - same classifier, same two diagnostics. Fixed on the way: the AOT-ledger carrier now opens HEADER-ONLY (the ledger is a container-global segment, but the probe ran complete_open, which binds the frozen string pool and arena into LIVE parse state - it died with 'forest thaw requires a live string pool' in a lane with no lexer). New -fno-eval-shims: every .o carries __madc_shim_* host-call adapters whose twelve madc_value_* imports are Tier B, an executable emit from source skips them and a .o cannot know, so the build says it (the -fPIC shape). Fork unchanged (1.0-madc.0.52.0 @ba216dea).

READ THIS WHOLE ENTRY, THEN docs/plans/2026-07-26-libcxx-flavor-plan.md. === 1. RELEASED v0.53.0 (develop @9af72c00, master stays v0.48.0, fork UNCHANGED 1.0-madc.0.52.0 @ba216dea -- no new fork tag). -static-libmadc now works in the .o LINK lane: the runtime is pulled into a PRIVATE object-mode context, generated, emitted with MIR_gen_object_emit, and merged into the input builder via MIR_object_read. NOT generated into the capture as the #10 handoff guessed -- a builder's symbol table is APPEND-ONLY (MIR_object_add_symbol never dedupes), so unification only happens in the MERGE. New -fno-eval-shims because every .o keeps __madc_shim_* host-call adapters whose 12 madc_value_* imports are Tier B; `-static-libmadc -shared` from source refuses IDENTICALLY (pre-existing) = task #26. Gates: forest_ledger_gate 14->19 checks, fulltest 756/0/0/9, --exe 740/0, --obj 740/0, machogate 30/30, packed 756/0/0/9. === 2. THE CONTAINER WAS REBUILT FROM A BASE IMAGE (WSL crash). /workspace (the volume) survived; everything apt-installed in the old container's overlay did NOT. THE LOSS READS AS GREEN because macho_obj_gate SKIPS without llvm-18/SDK. FIX, now in the repo: bash scripts/provision_container.sh (idempotent; --check reports only; it never installs the owner's macOS SDK, only reports it). Two traps it encodes: libxqdbm-dev is a SEPARATE package from libqdbm-dev (first reconfigure silently came back xqdbm=0), and the gates need the UNVERSIONED clang/clang++ (class_pattern_equivalence refuses loudly without it -- that is how it was found). After any container rebuild: run that script, then autoconf + ./configure IN THE CONTAINER (configure is generated/untracked and the NAS's stale copy is pushed over the container's by sync). Restored env re-verified green end to end. === 3. OWNER CORRECTION THAT RESHAPED P2: libc++ is a STANDARD LIBRARY, NOT A PLATFORM (Apple, the Android NDK, FreeBSD, clang-on-Linux). So the track is madc's SECOND STDLIB FLAVOR selected by `-stdlib=` (clang's spelling), with darwin as its first consumer; never key C++ library behavior off 'is the target Apple'. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the library work is developed and GATED ON LINUX against libc++-18-dev with clang++-18 as the oracle -- no Mac needed; hardware only proves the darwin target plumbing. (b) the inline ABI namespace must be READ from the parsed __config (_LIBCPP_ABI_NAMESPACE, verified to expand to __1 here but versioned and vendor-variable), never written as a literal -- same as libstdc++'s __cxx11 following _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI. Doc renamed to docs/plans/2026-07-26-libcxx-flavor-plan.md. === 4. P2.1 DONE AND GATED (committed 91f36724 on feature/libcxx-flavor-claude): madc bakes TWO tables from $(CXX) at build time -- the #include search list AND the predefined macros. The cross-macos MODEs baked Linux paths and predefined __linux__ with NO __APPLE__/__MACH__, which no header search could fix because libc++'s __config branches on those. New HOSTTAB_CXX (defaults to $(CXX); cross Apple MODEs override to the darwin clang) drives BOTH generators. Also DARWIN_CXX_ISYS (-nostdinc++ -isystem $(MACOS_SDK)/usr/include/c++/v1) on cross AND hosted: installing libc++-18-dev on the build host makes clang prefer its OWN libc++ over the SDK's, which would have silently mis-compiled the HOSTED darwin binaries too; -isysroot alone does NOT fix it. Verified: SDK c++/v1 first, __APPLE__/__MACH__/__aarch64__ present, machogate 30/30, native rebuild regenerates the Linux tables (no cross-contamination). === 5. BURN-DOWN MEASURED, and it is much smaller than it first looked. libc++ 18 references 59 distinct __has_builtin names (41 are type-trait intrinsics), BUT its __type_traits/ has exactly TWO hard #errors: remove_reference and is_trivially_destructible. Everything else has C++ fallbacks. So the critical path is __has_builtin + TWO intrinsics; the other 39 are a later speed pass. Expect the real burn-down to land in TEMPLATE METAPROGRAMMING (the fallbacks) on the tsubst spine, not in intrinsics. === 6. SLICE 1 WRITTEN, UNCOMMITTED, BATTERY IN FLIGHT. Files: src/lexer.cpp + include/madc.h (Program::has_builtin + Program::evaluateHasQuery + the expandIfMacros operand protection) and the plan doc. The __has_* family are real operators now: __has_builtin answers from the 138-entry define_map alias table (which IS madc's implementation for that family; -fno-builtin does NOT change the answer, matching clang), __has_include/__has_include_next answer through the SAME resolver #include uses, and the other six parse their operand and answer 0 DELIBERATELY (madc supports a real subset but has no registry to ask; an unbacked yes would trade a library's clean #error for a mystifying failure). THE BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: #if operands are macro-expanded first and madc aliases 138 builtins, so __has_builtin(__builtin_memcpy) arrived as __has_builtin(memcpy) and answered NO for a builtin madc has; `defined` was already protected, the __has_* family now is too (whole parenthesized group). Verified 4/4 on known-true/known-false cases. NOTE THIS HAS REACH BEYOND THE TRACK: #if __has_include(...) can now be TRUE in any compile, so headers that took fallback paths now take real ones -- that is why the whole battery is running. TO FINISH: read /workspace/madc/tmp/hq-summary in the container (fulltest + --exe + --obj). If green, commit; if not, the failures are the price of the __has_include truth-telling and must be fixed, not reverted. === 7. NEXT SLICE (P2.2b), already diagnosed: with honest answers the Linux libc++ probe stops at `cstddef:50: #error <cstddef> tried including <stddef.h> but didn't find libc++'s <stddef.h>`. madc embeds the freestanding set (stddef/stdint/limits/float/stdarg/stdbool) and libc++ ships ITS OWN wrappers for several of those names, which must be found FIRST (they #include_next the C library's). madc's embedded copies shadow them. Clang's order settles the design: c++/v1 -> compiler resource dir -> C library, where madc's embedded set IS the resource dir -- so embedded headers must become a FALLBACK for names a real search path cannot satisfy (which also preserves the header-less-Mac promise and is the precedence P2.4's frozen groves need). The darwin lane hits the same wall after its trait blocker; fixing it here fixes it there. === 8. RECON TREES (owner reminder): /workspace/gcc (full) and /workspace/llvm-clang-src -- but the clang checkout is PARTIAL: clang/lib has only AST and Sema (good for trait-intrinsic semantics), there is NO clang/lib/Lex, so header-search ordering must come from behavior + docs. === 9. PROBE FIXTURES in the container: tmp/p2probe.cpp (#include <string> + printf), tmp/hasq.c (the __has_* truth table). Darwin lane: bin/madc-arm64-macos -c -o tmp/x.o tmp/p2probe.cpp. Linux libc++ lane (until -stdlib= exists): bin/madc -I/usr/lib/llvm-18/include/c++/v1 -c -o tmp/x.o tmp/p2probe.cpp. === STANDING: QNAP never builds/tests (container ssh -p 2299 dev@localhost does ALL; payloads need an explicit cd /workspace/madc); rsync/remote_build.sh sync; git commit -F; NEVER git add -A (untracked files here are MY generated leftovers, not owner WIP); cap every test run; ONE heavy container job at a time (detached nohup + rc-file waiter, rm the rc file first); CLI flags BEFORE inputs; A QUESTION IS NEVER A DIRECTIVE; the macOS SDK is NEVER committed or synced; configure is generated/untracked (autoconf in the container AFTER the last sync); scope test runs by BLAST RADIUS and give a GROUP one battery; release cadence = a feature merge to develop comes WITH a release (docs/infra commits exempt). REHYDRATE: scripts/resume.sh -> this live_handoff -> docs/plans/2026-07-26-libcxx-flavor-plan.md -> finish slice 1 (item 6), then P2.2b (item 7).

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.

MadArray/MadValue namespacing is an open API/ABI follow-up: moving the real C++ types to madc::array and madc::value would give PHP array helpers a normal namespace type surface, but compatibility aliases alone will not preserve old C++ mangled names.
